SUMMARY.md: "scripture": read as sacred by its tradition. "classic": a story, history, or teaching that is not read as scripture. "recorded": an oral tradition that an outside observer wrote down.
A URI that names the error type.

An API and MCP server for the Urantia Papers. Structured access to all 197 papers and more than 14,500 paragraphs, with full-text and semantic search, named entities, cross-references to public domain texts of the world's religions, and audio. No key needed. Docs: https://docs.urantia.dev
Bible verse with top-10 UB paragraphs
Corpus id, slug, or ref prefix, for example

For a concept with a lowercase name: "special" when the papers coin the word or use it in their own sense, "ordinary" when they use it in its everyday sense. A reader app can leave ordinary words out of a list of terms. Null for other entries.
How far this text's percentile is above the paragraph's mean across texts

How the paragraph matched: reference (the query named it), exact (the whole phrase), all (every word), near (every word after a typo fix, see meta.didYouMean), most (two thirds of the words or more; with type `or`, some of the words).
How the text is numbered or selected
Mean percentile across the texts, 0 to 1
Number of citations in the source index. A citation of a whole section counts once, so the entity's paragraph total can be higher.
Present only when the text is a translation: a machine made it, and it is released as CC0. No person has reviewed it.
Related entry names. An entity with citationCount 0 is a cross-reference stub: follow seeAlso to the entry that has the paragraphs.
The passage with its top 10 Urantia paragraphs
The prefix of its references, such as "Dhp". Null for the Bible (a book name).
The short name of the status.
